275	## Common Topology Patterns
276	
277	Use these as building blocks when designing your flow.
278	
279	### Linear Pipeline
280	
281	```
282	Trigger -> Action A -> Action B -> Action C -> End
283	```
284	
285	### Conditional Branch
286	
287	```
288	Trigger -> Fetch Data -> Decision
289	  |-- true -> Process -> End
290	  |-- false -> Log Skip -> End
291	```
292	
293	### Parallel Execution with Merge
294	
295	```
296	Trigger -> Prepare
297	  |-- Call API A --+
298	  |-- Call API B --+
299	                   +-- Merge -> Combine -> End
300	```
301	
302	### Loop Over Collection
303	
304	```
305	Trigger -> Fetch List -> Loop
306	  |-- [loop body] Process Item -> (loopBack)
307	  |-- success -> Summarize -> End
308	```
309	
310	### Error Handling (implicit `error` port)
311	
312	Wire the action node's implicit `error` source port directly to a handler — this catches node-level failures (network errors, timeouts, non-2xx HTTP responses, script exceptions, transform faults). Do NOT put a Decision downstream to check for errors — by the time execution reaches the Decision, a failing node has already faulted the flow.
313	
314	```
315	Trigger -> HTTP Request
316	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success)
317	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (error path with descriptive output)
318	```
319	
320	Use a downstream Decision/Switch only for **content-based routing on a successful response** (e.g., `items.length > 0`), not as a failure detector. HTTP also supports `inputs.branches` for that. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — the `Error port vs other branching` table spells out when to use each.
321	
322	**Plan the error edge in Phase 1.** If the requirements mention "if the call fails", "invalid input", "article not found", or any failure fallback, add an edge from the action node's `error` port to a handler in the edge table — don't leave it to the build step.
323	
324	### Orchestration (Mixed Resources)
325	
326	The canonical composition when more than one product is in play. Default division of labor — most "where does this step go?" questions resolve against it:
327	
328	> **RPA = hands. Maestro = conductor. Agents = brain. Humans approve.**
329	
330	- **Maestro orchestrates** — owns the case, the waits, the branching, the SLA, the long-running state (this flow).
331	- **RPA executes** — mechanical work against systems with no clean API (desktop apps, terminals, legacy web) — a `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*` resource node. See [rpa/planning.md](plugins/rpa/planning.md).
332	- **Agents reason** — judgment calls: classify, summarize, decide which branch a fuzzy input belongs to — an agent node. See [agent/planning.md](plugins/agent/planning.md) / [inline-agent/planning.md](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md).
333	- **Humans approve** — a HITL / human-task node wraps the point where a person must look before the case continues. See [hitl/planning.md](plugins/hitl/planning.md).
334	
335	Worked example — extract, classify, and route with one human approval branch:
336	
337	```
338	Trigger -> Script (prepare) -> RPA Process (extract from legacy app) -> Agent (classify) -> Decision (confidence high)
339	  |-- true  -> Script (format) -> End (auto-approved)
340	  |-- false -> HITL (human approves or rejects) -> Decision (approved)
341	                 |-- true  -> Script (format) -> End (approved)
342	                 |-- false -> Script (log rejection) -> End (rejected)
343	```
344	
345	Here Maestro holds the case across the agent call and the human wait; RPA does the extraction the source app gives no API for; the agent makes the confidence call; the human is the gate only when the agent is unsure. Each non-Maestro piece is a separate published (or in-solution) artifact the flow references as a node — you do **not** rebuild them inside the flow.
346	
347	### Scheduled Batch Processing
348	
349	```
350	Scheduled Trigger -> HTTP (fetch batch) -> Loop
351	  |-- Queue Create (per item) -> (loopBack)
352	  |-- success -> Script (summary) -> End
353	```
354	
355	### No-API Source (RPA Feeder Bridge)
356	
357	When the source application has **no API and no connector** (legacy desktop app, terminal, mainframe screen), the flow cannot be triggered by the source directly. Bridge it: a **scheduled RPA bot scrapes the source and drops the result onto something Maestro can watch** — a Queue or a Storage Bucket — and the flow triggers off that.
358	
359	```
360	[Scheduled RPA bot]  (outside the flow — uipath-rpa + a time trigger)
361	   scrape legacy app -> push item to Queue (or file to Bucket)
362	        |
363	        v
364	Queue/Bucket item created
365	        |
366	        v
367	Maestro flow trigger -> Process item -> ... -> End
368	```
369	
370	Two ways to wire the Maestro side:
371	
372	- **Queue → flow:** the RPA bot calls `Add Queue Item`; the flow is started by a queue trigger (configured in Orchestrator — see [/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform)) or polls/consumes the queue. Best when each scraped row is a separate case.
373	- **Bucket → flow:** the RPA bot uploads a file; a scheduled flow picks it up. Best for batch drops.
374	
375	> **Tradeoff — polling latency equals the scraper schedule.** The case starts no sooner than the next RPA run. A bot scheduled every 15 minutes means up to 15 minutes of trigger latency. There is no event from a no-API source, so "real-time" is not achievable this way — tighten the RPA schedule to lower latency, at the cost of more bot runs. If the source *does* expose an event/webhook or has a connector, prefer a connector trigger ([connector-trigger/planning.md](plugins/connector-trigger/planning.md)) over this bridge.
376	
377	The scraper bot itself is an RPA project ([/uipath:uipath-rpa](/uipath:uipath-rpa)) with a time trigger ([/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform)); only the consuming flow belongs to this skill.
378	
379	---
380	
381	## Output Format
382	
383	Generate a `<SolutionName>.uipath.flow.arch.plan.md` file in the **solution directory** (the folder containing the `.uipx` file, not the project subfolder). The plan covers the entire solution — which may contain multiple projects in the future.
384	
385	### 1. Summary
386	
387	2-3 sentences describing what the flow does end-to-end.
388	
389	### 2. Flow Diagram (Mermaid)
390	
391	A mermaid flowchart showing all nodes, edges, and branching logic.
392	
393	**Requirements:**
394	
395	- Use `graph LR` (left-right) for all flows — Flow uses a horizontal canvas. Do NOT use `graph TD` (top-down) — it produces vertical diagrams that conflict with the horizontal node layout. Do NOT use `flowchart` — it is not supported by all mermaid renderers.
396	- Use `subgraph` blocks to group related sections — required for flows with 10+ nodes
397	- Label every edge with the port name (e.g., `-->|success|`, `-->|true|`, `-->|false|`)
398	- **Labels must be plain text only** — no special characters inside shape delimiters. The following break mermaid parsing:
399	  - `>` and `<` (interpreted as shape operators or HTML) — replace with words like "over" or "under"
400	  - `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` (conflict with shape delimiters)
401	  - `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `"` (unreliable across renderers)
402	  - Use plain alphanumeric text and spaces only
403	- Do NOT put node types in diagram labels — node types belong in the Node Table only
404	- Do NOT use quotes inside shape delimiters — use `[Text]` not `["Text"]`
405	- Use only these universally supported node shapes:
406	  - Triggers: rounded rectangle `(Trigger Name)`
407	  - Actions: rectangle `[Action Name]`
408	  - Control flow: diamond `{Decision Name}` for Decision/Switch
409	  - End/Terminate: rounded rectangle `(Done)`
410	  - Connectors: rectangle `[Connector Service Operation]`
411	  - Placeholders: rectangle `[Mock Description]`
412	
413	**Example:**
414	
415	````markdown
416	```mermaid
417	graph LR
418	    trigger(Manual Trigger)
419	    fetchOrders[Fetch Orders]
420	    checkHasOrders{Any Orders}
421	    processOrder[Process Order]
422	    notifySlack[Slack Send Message]
423	    logSkip[Log Skip]
424	    logError[Log Error]
425	    doneSuccess(Done)
426	    doneSkip(Done)
427	    doneError(Done Error)
428	    trigger -->|output| fetchOrders
429	    fetchOrders -->|default| checkHasOrders
430	    fetchOrders -->|error| logError
431	    checkHasOrders -->|true| processOrder
432	    checkHasOrders -->|false| logSkip
433	    processOrder -->|success| notifySlack
434	    notifySlack -->|success| doneSuccess
435	    logSkip -->|success| doneSkip
436	    logError -->|success| doneError
437	```
438	````

440	### 3. Node Table
441	
442	| # | Node ID | Name | Category | Node Type | Inputs | Outputs | Notes |
443	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
444	| 1 | trigger | Manual Trigger | trigger | `core.trigger.manual` | — | Trigger event | — |
445	| 2 | fetchOrders | Fetch Orders | action | `core.action.http.v2` | `method: GET`, `url: <ORDERS_API_URL>` | `output.body` (order list), `error` (on HTTP failure) | Phase 2: confirm URL and auth |
446	| 3 | checkHasOrders | Any Orders | control | `core.logic.decision` | `expression: $vars.fetchOrders.output.body.length > 0` | Routes to `true` or `false` | — |
447	| 4 | logError | Log Error | action | `core.action.script` | `script: return { message: $vars.fetchOrders.error.message };` | `output.message` | Handles failed HTTP call |
448	
449	**Column definitions:**
450	
451	- **Node ID**: Short camelCase identifier used in the mermaid diagram and edge table
452	- **Inputs**: Best-guess input values based on user requirements. Use `<PLACEHOLDER>` for values Phase 2 must resolve (URLs, IDs, connection details)
453	- **Outputs**: What downstream nodes are expected to consume via `$vars.{nodeId}.*`

458	| # | Source Node | Source Port | Target Node | Target Port | Condition/Label |
459	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

497	
498	## Mermaid Validation Rules
499	
500	LLM-generated mermaid frequently contains syntax errors. After generating the diagram, **check every rule below** before presenting it to the user. Fix violations before outputting.
501	
502	### Syntax Rules
503	
504	1. **First line must be `graph LR`** (horizontal — matches the Flow canvas) — use `graph` not `flowchart` (the `flowchart` keyword is not supported by all renderers).
505	2. **Node IDs must be alphanumeric + underscores only** — no hyphens, dots, or spaces in IDs. Use `fetchData` not `fetch-data` or `fetch.data`
506	3. **Node IDs must not start with or equal a reserved word** — mermaid reserves these as keywords: `end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`. IDs that start with these (e.g., `endWarm`, `defaultPath`, `styleNode`) break the parser. Use alternatives like `warmEnd`, `pathDefault`, `nodeStyle` — or use a prefix like `done_warm`, `finish_warm`.
507	4. **Node labels must be plain text** — no quotes inside shape delimiters. Use `A[Fetch Data]` not `A["Fetch Data"]`.
508	5. **No special characters in labels** — these break mermaid parsing even when quoted:
509	   - `>` and `<` (interpreted as shape operators or HTML) — replace with words like "over" or "under"
510	   - `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` (conflict with shape delimiters)
511	   - `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `"` (unreliable across renderers)
512	   - Use plain alphanumeric text and spaces only
513	6. **Use only universally supported shapes** — `(text)` for rounded rectangle, `[text]` for rectangle, `{text}` for diamond. Do NOT use `([text])` (stadium), `{{text}}` (hexagon), or other extended shapes — they are not supported by all renderers.
514	7. **Edge labels use `|label|` between arrow and target** — `A -->|success| B` not `A -->success B` or `A --success--> B`
515	8. **No empty labels** — `A --> B` is fine, but `A -->|| B` is invalid
516	9. **Subgraph IDs must be unique** and not collide with node IDs
517	10. **Subgraph blocks must be closed** — every `subgraph` needs a matching `end`
518	11. **No semicolons** — mermaid uses newlines, not semicolons, to separate statements
519	12. **No blank lines inside the mermaid block** — blank lines between node definitions and edges can prevent rendering in some mermaid implementations. Keep all lines contiguous.
520	
521	### Structural Rules
522	
523	1. **Every node defined must be connected** — no orphan nodes floating in the diagram
524	2. **Edge directions must match the flow** — trigger at the top, End at the bottom (for TB layouts)
525	3. **Decision nodes must show both branches** — `true` and `false` edges, each labeled
526	4. **Switch nodes must show all case edges** — one per case plus optional default
527	5. **Loop structures**: show the loop body and the loopBack edge returning to the loop node
528	6. **Parallel branches** must visually fork from one node and converge at a Merge node
529	
530	### Validation Procedure
531	
532	After generating the mermaid block:
533	
534	1. First line is `graph LR` — not `flowchart`
535	2. Check each node ID contains only `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`
536	3. Check no node ID starts with or equals a reserved word (`end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`)
537	4. Check no labels contain `>`, `<`, `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `(`, `)`, or quotes — replace with plain words
538	5. Only `(text)`, `[text]`, and `{text}` shapes are used — no `([text])`, `{{text}}`, or other extended shapes
539	6. Check each edge has valid `-->`, `-->|label|` syntax
540	7. Check all subgraphs are closed
541	8. Verify every node in the node table appears in the diagram
542	9. Verify every edge in the edge table appears in the diagram
543	10. Check for blank lines inside the mermaid block — remove any empty lines between statements
544	11. If any rule is violated, fix it before outputting
545	
546	---
547	
548	## Node Selection Heuristics
549	
550	Quick decision guide. For full details, read the linked plugin's `planning.md`.
551	
552	### "I need to call an external service"
553	
554	1. Is there a connector with a curated activity? Run `uip maestro flow registry list --output json` and check for typed nodes matching `uipath.connector.<key>.<operation>`. If the desired operation appears as a node type, it is a curated activity -> [connector](plugins/connector/planning.md)
555	2. Connector exists but the operation is not listed as a curated node type? -> `core.action.http.v2` connector mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
556	3. No connector exists, but has a REST API? -> `core.action.http.v2` manual mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
557	4. No API at all (desktop app, terminal)? -> [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if unpublished
558	
559	### "I need to branch"
560	
561	- Two paths -> [decision](plugins/decision/planning.md)
562	- Three or more paths -> [switch](plugins/switch/planning.md)
563	- Branch on HTTP response status -> [http](plugins/http/planning.md) built-in branches
564	
565	### "I need to transform data"
566	
567	- Standard map/filter/group-by -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
568	- Custom logic, string manipulation, computation -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md)
569	
570	### "I need to end the flow"
571	
572	- Normal completion -> [end](plugins/end/planning.md) (one per terminal path)
573	- Fatal error, abort everything -> [terminate](plugins/terminate/planning.md)
574	
575	### "I need to wait"
576	
577	- Fixed duration -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
578	- Wait until a specific time -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
579	- Wait for external work to complete -> [queue](plugins/queue/planning.md) (`create-and-wait`)
580	
581	### "I need human involvement"
582	
583	- Human approval or data entry -> [hitl](plugins/hitl/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if the app doesn't exist
584	
585	### "I need an AI agent"
586	
587	- Low-code agent tightly coupled to this flow, bundled inside the flow project -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) (`uipath.agent.autonomous`)
588	- Coded (Python) agent, or any agent that lives as a separate project (in this solution or published to Orchestrator) -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`)
589	
590	### "I need an LLM to process rows of a CSV or summarize a document"
591	
592	- Add LLM-generated columns to every row of a CSV (classify, summarize, extract) -> [batch-transform](plugins/batch-transform/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.batch-transform`)
593	- Synthesize or answer questions over one attached document, with optional citations -> [summarize](plugins/summarize/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.deep-rag`)
594	- Small ad-hoc reshaping (map/filter/groupBy) without an LLM -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
595	- Multi-step reasoning with tool use -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) or [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md)
596	
597	### "I need to extract structured fields from documents"
598	
599	- Source is a PDF, scanned form, photo, or email attachment with **variable layout** across inputs (invoices from many vendors, receipts, contracts, forms) -> [ixp](plugins/ixp/planning.md) (`uipath.ixp.{modelName}.{fullyQualifiedName}`)

602	- IxP model not yet trained -> use `core.logic.mock` and surface in Open Questions

604	### "The flow needs something outside flow capabilities"

606	1. Add a `core.logic.mock` placeholder
607	2. Note what needs to be created and which skill handles it:
608	   - Desktop/browser automation or coded workflow (C#) -> `uipath-rpa`

1	# Connector Activity Nodes — Implementation
2	
3	How to configure connector activity nodes: connection binding, enriched metadata, reference field resolution, and debugging. Connection bindings are emitted by `uip maestro flow node configure` into the flow's top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from them at debug/pack time and should never be hand-edited.
4	
5	For generic node/edge add, remove, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). This guide covers the connector-specific configuration workflow that must follow the generic node add.
6	
7	## How Connector Nodes Differ from OOTB
8	
9	1. **Connection binding required** — every connector node needs an IS connection (OAuth, API key, etc.) authored in the flow's top-level `bindings[]` (which the CLI regenerates into `bindings_v2.json` at debug/pack time). Without it, the node cannot authenticate.
10	2. **Enriched metadata via `--connection-id`** — call `registry get` with `--connection-id` to get connection-aware field metadata. Without it, only base fields are returned — custom fields, dynamic enums, and reference resolution are missing.
11	3. **`inputs.detail` object** — connector nodes store operation-specific configuration in `inputs.detail`, populated by `uip maestro flow node configure`:
12	   - `connectionId` — the bound IS connection UUID
13	   - `connectionFolderKey` — the Orchestrator folder key in the authored `.flow` file. `node configure --detail` accepts `folderKey` as input and writes it back as `connectionFolderKey`.
14	   - `method` — HTTP method from `registry get` → `connectorMethodInfo.method` (e.g., `POST`)
15	   - `endpoint` — API path. Read `connectorMethodInfo.path` (from `registry get`) or `availableOperations[].path` (from `is resources describe`).
16	   - `objectName` — required for generic activities (see below). The API object name (e.g. `"Opportunity"`); ignored for concrete nodes.
17	   - `bodyParameters` — field-value pairs for the request body. Read field names from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`).
18	   - `queryParameters` — field-value pairs for query string parameters. Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: query` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
19	   - `pathParameters` — field-value pairs for path placeholders in `endpoint` (e.g. `{conversationsInfoId}`). Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: path` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
20	   - `filter` — structured FilterBuilder tree for list/query operations. See Step 6a.
21	   - `customFieldsRequestDetails` — design-time cache for connectors with an api-type ObjectAction at top-level `objectActions[]` OR `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`). camelCase keys; `parameterValues` as `[key, value]` tuples. See Step 6c.
22	   - `multipartParameters` — derived from IS metadata params where `type === "multipart"`. Array of `{name, dataType, value?}`. Pass file values via `--detail.bodyParameters.<name>`; `node configure` moves file-typed values into the matching `multipartParameters[i].value` slot (matched by `name`). String-typed entries — including the body aggregator field whose name is given by `inputMetadata.multipart.bodyFieldName` — stay in `bodyParameters`.
23	   - `inputMetadata` — auto-derived. `{type: "multipart", multipart: {bodyFieldName}}` when multipart params exist; `{operation: "list", pagination: {maxPageSize}}` for list operations. Driven by `methodInfo.parameters` + `methodInfo.operation`.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Generic vs Concrete Activities
28	
29	Connector nodes come in two flavors:
30	
31	- **Concrete** — the node type encodes a specific object + operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-atlassian-jira.curated_create_issue`). `inputDefinition.fields[]` is populated; `method` and `endpoint` are fixed.
32	- **Generic** — the node type encodes only the operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-sfdc.list-records`, `…insert-record`, `…update-record`). `inputDefinition` is `{}`; the node needs an extra `objectName` in `--detail`, and `method` / `endpoint` come from `is resources describe`.
33	
34	To classify a node, read `Node.form.sections[0].fields[0].componentProps.connectorDetail.configuration` from the `registry get` response, parse it as JSON, and check `activityType`. `"Generic"` → run Step 2a to discover `objectName` (and capture `operation` from the same marker for the `--operation` flag in Step 3). Anything else → skip Step 2a.
35	
36	
37	## Critical: Connector Definition Must Include `form`
38	
39	> Connector definitions in `definitions[]` are CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)) — `uip maestro flow node add` copies them verbatim from the registry, and you should never hand-write or hand-edit them. If `node configure` fails with `No instanceParameters found in definition`, the definition in `definitions[]` is missing the `form` field — typically because the local registry cache is stale (the definition was copied in before the CLI started emitting `form`). Recovery: `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`, delete the stale `definitions[]` entry, re-run `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type>` so the CLI re-copies the definition with `form`. Do not paste `form` in by hand — re-running `node add` is the supported path.
40	
41	## No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration
42	
43	If you cannot run `node configure` (no live connection, sandbox forbids it, the user asked for planning only):
44	
45	1. Confirm the connector operation exists: `uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>` and `registry get <node-type>` (see [cli-commands.md — registry](../../../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-registry) for the `search` output shape).
46	2. Add the connector node with `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type> --output json`. This is still required — it inserts the node and copies the definition into `definitions[]`.
47	3. Write the planned `--detail` payload to a separate file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`) with placeholder values for missing connection/folder UUIDs. Do **not** put a partial `inputs.detail` on the node.
48	4. **The node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run.** Surface this explicitly in your completion report under "Missing connections" or "Open questions" — do not let the user discover it via a validation failure later.
49	
50	Do not replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run. Mocks are only for genuinely unknown, unpublished, or not-yet-built non-connector resources. A real connector node added via `node add` but unconfigured preserves the registered connector key that Studio Web, reviewers, and downstream tooling need.
51	
52	When piping `--output json` into `python`, `jq`, or another parser, do not merge stderr into stdout. The CLI may emit diagnostic lines such as "Tool factory already registered..." before the JSON on stderr; use `2>/dev/null` for parse-only probes or capture stderr separately.
53	
54	## Configuration Workflow
55	
56	Follow these steps for every connector node.
57	
58	### Step 1 — Fetch and bind a connection
59	
60	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity-name>`).
61	
62	Discovery call is **always**:
63	
64	```bash
65	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
66	```
67	
68	`connections list` returns `Data` as a flat array. Do **not** parse `Data.Connections` or `Data.Items`; those wrapper objects are not part of the CLI JSON contract. Read each candidate from `Data[]` and use PascalCase fields:
69	
70	```json
71	{
72	  "Data": [
73	    {
74	      "Id": "<connection-id>",
75	      "Name": "<display-name>",
76	      "State": "Enabled",

success_criteria:
  # What this checks: did the agent search the registry for IxP nodes?
  # Passes (case-insensitive) when the agent ran either:
  #   • `registry list`                   — list all nodes, or
  #   • `registry search|list|get <term>` — <term> contains ixp / document / extract
  #                                         (prefix match, so extract → extraction)
  # routing_listing.yaml drops `get` (read-only). Keep in sync with
  # scaffold_minimal.yaml, scaffold_multinode.yaml, routing_listing.yaml.
  - type: command_executed
    description: "Agent searched the registry for IxP node types"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(?i)uip\s+maestro\s+flow\s+registry\s+(list\b|(search|list|get)\b[^\n]*\b(ixp|document|extract))'
    min_count: 1
    suite_thresholds: {mean: 0.85}

  # Greps the actual .flow artifact rather than the command stream — the
  # command_executed checker truncates tool params at 2000 chars, which hides
  # `"type": "core.logic.mock"` when the agent writes a large flow file in a
  # single Write call.  Per references/plugins/ixp/impl.md, the agent must land
  # either an `uipath.ixp.*` node or a `core.logic.mock` placeholder.
  - type: run_command
    description: "Agent added an IxP or core.logic.mock placeholder node to a .flow file (per references/plugins/ixp/impl.md)"
    command: 'grep -rqE "\"type\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"(uipath\.ixp|core\.logic\.mock)" --include="*.flow" .'
    expected_exit_code: 0
    suite_thresholds: {mean: 0.85}
